correctness.rationale: Valuation layers \(V_i=\mathfrak m^i\setminus\mathfrak m^{i+1}\) are nonempty and satisfy \(xy=0\) exactly when \(i+j\ge\ell\). The \((\ell-1)\times(\ell-1)\) layer matrix \(H_{ij}=1_{i+j\ge\ell}\) becomes triangular with unit diagonal after reversing columns, hence has rank \(\ell-1\). Inflating it through the layer-incidence matrix gives a real symmetric graph-pattern matrix of the same rank. Leaving one white representative in each valuation layer gives a forcing chain from low layers to high layers and finally back to \(V_1\), so \(Z\le N-(\ell-1)\); \(M\le Z\) closes the equality. Fresh exact reconstruction reproduced the claimed \((Z,\operatorname{rank})\) for \((q,\ell)=(3,2),(2,3),(3,3),(2,4)\), including exhaustive zero forcing in those small cases.
correctness.risk: The result is for standard zero-divisor graphs and real symmetric minimum rank; it does not classify all minimum forcing sets.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly recovers a ring's nilpotency length from a graph inverse-eigenvalue parameter and proves simultaneous equality with zero forcing/maximum nullity throughout the finite chain-ring family. The anti-triangular layer witness is a structural mechanism that is reusable beyond one numerical example.
value.risk: The theorem is restricted to chain rings and does not address arbitrary local rings with multidimensional valuation layers.

final_claim: For a finite commutative chain ring with residue-field order \(q\) and nilpotency length \(\ell\ge2\), the nonzero zero-divisor graph has \(Z=M=q^{\ell-1}-\ell\) and real symmetric minimum rank \(\ell-1\), except at \((q,\ell)=(2,2)\), where the graph is \(K_1\), \(Z=M=1\), and \(\operatorname{mr}=0\).
limitations: No classification of all minimum zero forcing sets is claimed.
